title: Talking Back: Input and Type Conversion

ai_pair_moment.flaw: The AI forgot to convert the answer from input() and predicted 'Change: 7.50'. With the answer 30, Python stopped with TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'str' and 'float'. Wrapping input() in float() fixes it.

changes: Added str() as a small extra beside int() and float(), so learners know the conversion in both directions.

Examples that read input use .stdin files. tools/verify_chapter.py now echoes each typed answer after its prompt for Python, so every expected output shows the terminal exactly as the learner sees it.
Answer checking (if, try and except) is left to later chapters; Mistake 3 tells the learner to make the prompt say what to type for now.
outstanding_issues: The tracebacks in Common mistakes show the short file name; on a learner's computer the full path to the file appears instead.
The narration uses a synthetic voice (Kokoro bm_lewis). The owner should watch the video once and flag any word the voice mispronounces; fixes go in the PRONOUNCE list in tools/voice.py.
